scan_notes: Reviewed the three named commits separately from the develop merges, plus current surrounding code, production caller, build_page renderer path, tests, and measurement tool. `git status --short` showed no tracked or untracked changes. The marker spelling, positive per-trace test, production trace markings, unmarked-trace behavior, and old-rule version refusal appear correct. The repository fact-check passed for all three commits. Per the read-only constraint, pytest was not run; runtime outcomes below are static inferences from the code.

findings.title: Renderer checks only the longest marked trace
findings.evidence: The renderer validates only the pooled maximum: `to = rc.get("projected_to")` followed by `if not _beyond_edge(str(to), tg, value, grain)`. The resolver instead checks every member of `census["marked"]`, but records only `projected_to` as the longest trace. Static inference; tests could not be executed.
findings.failure_scenario: For an edge of `2026-05`, use two marked traces: one ending `2029-07` and a mis-marked actual ending `2026-05`. `refuse_edge_beyond_rendered` refuses because the second trace is not strictly later. A current-rule JSON record with nonzero counts and `projected_to: "2029-07"` passes `rendered_check_problem`, so `build_page.py` can render a record the resolver would refuse.
findings.suggested_fix: Record per-trace latest period and grain—or at least the weakest trace selected with the same period ordering—and make `rendered_check_problem` apply `_beyond_edge` to every recorded trace. Add the two-trace resolver-versus-renderer test.

findings.title: No-period verdict accepts a record reporting excluded traces
findings.evidence: The contradiction check only rejects `no-period-axis` when `periods_before_exclusion > 0`; it ignores `excluded_traces`. The later branch then unconditionally returns `None` for `no-period-axis`. Static inference; tests could not be executed.
findings.failure_scenario: A current-rule record with `verdict: "no-period-axis"`, `periods_before_exclusion: 0`, `excluded_traces: 1`, `periods_seen: 0`, and `latest_rendered: null` passes the renderer even though it explicitly reports that a trace was excluded. Such a record violates the invariant that projection exclusion must never produce `no-period-axis`.
findings.suggested_fix: For `no-period-axis`, require both exclusion counts to be zero, `periods_seen == 0`, and `latest_rendered is None`; otherwise refuse the record.

findings.title: Sweep can miss a verdict change when period arrays are equal
findings.evidence: Despite claiming to report verdict movement, the tool only evaluates `row["moved"] = sorted(b) != sorted(c["periods"])`; it never calls either revision's verdict resolver. It also compares lists rather than the sets claimed by the adjacent comment. Static inference; the database-backed sweep could not be run.
findings.failure_scenario: For one marked trace named `forecast`, both the old name rule and new marker rule exclude the same dates, so both surviving arrays are empty and the tool reports `moved=False`. The old resolver publishes `no-period-axis`, while the new resolver returns `all-projection` or refuses if the per-trace bound fails—exactly a verdict change the tool says it measures.
findings.suggested_fix: Resolve each page's declaration and compare the two modules' actual verdict/refusal outcomes. If the tool is intentionally limited to period membership, rename that claim and compare `set(b)` with `set(c["periods"])`.

overall_explanation: The production resolver enforces the new per-trace bound correctly, but the render-time second door discards the evidence needed to enforce it and can accept a record the resolver would reject. A second malformed-record path also violates the no-period-axis invariant. The measurement tool can additionally underreport verdict movement.
